title: Undeclared Origin
subtitle: The label does not say. That silence is the finding.
description: Most ingredients are not hidden. They are simply never explained.
stats_text: In our first analysis of real supermarket products, 72% of results could not be confirmed — not because the ingredients were forbidden, but because the label never declared where they came from.
stats_note: Based on BOTIA's own scans of supermarket products between March and April 2026, mostly in the Netherlands and Belgium, using the Muslim layer only. Repeated scans of the same product were counted once.
why_title: Why Mashbooh is the most important state
why_body: Classifying an ingredient as Mashbooh is not an accusation — it is a signal of uncertainty. Food labels are legal documents before they are human explanations. When the label omits the origin of an additive or the method of slaughter, BOTIA makes that gap visible so you can decide.
highlight_text: Scientific evidence works with what is declared. Personal choice needs to know where it came from. That is the difference — and that is where the label goes silent.
row1_general: Can be grouped by function without specifying vegetable or animal origin.
row1_halal: Requires all additives to come strictly from lawful sources.
row1_botia: If an additive could be animal-derived but the label is silent, BOTIA marks it as doubtful.
row2_halal: Requires lawful slaughter by a Muslim invoking Allah and cutting specific veins.
row2_botia: Labels almost never detail the slaughter method, so BOTIA cannot assume compliance.
ingredients_body: These are the ingredients BOTIA most often finds with undeclared origin. Any of them may be perfectly lawful — the label simply does not confirm it.
closing: Transparency is not certification. It is the right to know what the label says — and what it does not.
